data.body:
# Phase 2 complete — fix landed for review as Gerrit 1978

## Fix

`tests/conftest.py` — `_no_repo_root_leaks` no longer removes anything. The 11-line
cleanup loop (`shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)` / `target.unlink()` under
`except OSError: pass`) is gone; the fixture reports and fails only. In its place is a
comment stating why, addressed to whoever is tempted to restore it: a set difference proves
only that an entry APPEARED, deleting asserts "this test created it", and no obtainable
signal separates the two. The deletion is removed rather than made conditional because there
is nothing to condition it on — mtime, birthtime and name shape are each satisfied equally by
a legitimate concurrent write. `import shutil` drops out with it.

`tests/_isolation.py` — `leak_failure_message` gains one line before the existing two-cause
block: *"They were left on disk untouched — the guard removes nothing, so clean up yourself
once you know which cause applies."* Both existing clauses are byte-identical, so the
properties `test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py` pins (never asserts the test did it; always
offers the external-write cause) are preserved.

`docs/local-dev-env.md` — the detached-run section claimed "It also **deletes** what it
finds, so a file you create mid-run can disappear", which this change makes false. It now
says the guard reports only and that a genuine leak is the reader's to clean up. AC #4 is
also discharged there: the "do not work in that checkout" item now names `rebar` explicitly —
tracker writes land under the checkout (`.rebar/`, `.tickets-*`) and read as new entries, so
**running `rebar` against a worktree while its own suite runs is not supported**.

`_is_coverage_artifact`'s docstring was rewritten by the same change: its rationale was
written in the present tense around deletion, and the combine-corruption harm (story `8d36`)
is now recorded as history rather than as current behaviour.

## RED -> GREEN, with the oracle held out

`tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py` gains two tests that drive the **real** fixture —
resolved from the live plugin manager, not re-imported — against a `tmp_path` standing in for
REPO_ROOT, so the code under test is the shipped guard rather than the inline pytester copy:

* `test_leak_guard_leaves_entries_it_cannot_attribute_on_disk` — a concurrent writer creates
  a file AND a directory-with-contents mid-test; all three must survive teardown. Covers both
  removal branches.
* `test_leak_guard_still_fails_and_names_every_entry` — the guard must still fail, name every
  entry, and still tell an actually-leaking test to use `tmp_path`.

* **RED** on unmodified `main`, for the right reason:
  `AssertionError: the guard deleted a file it cannot attribute to the test` at the survival
  assertion (not an import or fixture error). The second test was green before and after, by
  design: it is the non-weakening guard.
* **Held out** — the test file was reverted to `main` and declared off-limits before the fix
  subagent started; the subagent reported it never opened it, and self-verified against its
  own scratch reproduction instead.
* **GREEN** after re-applying it: 18 passed across the guard self-test and the external-
  mutation diagnostics.
* **Mutation check** — re-introducing the exact confirmed root cause (the rmtree/unlink loop
  restored verbatim) returns the oracle to **RED** on the same assertion; restoring the fix
  returns it to GREEN. The test has teeth.
* **Refactoring litmus** — the assertions are observable postconditions (a path exists on
  disk; the failure text contains an entry name), not private names or a grep of source.

## AC #2 proven end-to-end as well, not only at the fixture level

A genuinely leaking test seeded into the worktree (`mkdir SEEDED_LEAK_dir` +
`write_text SEEDED_LEAK_file.txt` into REPO_ROOT), run through the real conftest:

    E  Failed: New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test:
       ['SEEDED_LEAK_dir', 'SEEDED_LEAK_file.txt']
    E  They were left on disk untouched — the guard removes nothing, ...
    1 passed, 1 error in 0.53s

Both entries named, and the debris was left on disk (then removed by hand) — the intended new
behaviour. This is not a silent weakening.

## Original report replicated

The Phase-1 reproduction re-run against the fix — external `touch` 8s into a 12s test body:

    1 passed, 1 error in 12.51s
    $ ls -la EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE
    -rw-r--r--  1 joeoakhart  staff  0 Aug 20 23:27 EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE

The file **survives**. The data-loss half of the report is gone. The innocent test is still
errored — that half is not fixable by attribution (the guard genuinely cannot tell), and it is
already mitigated by the message `f0fb` landed, which names the concurrent-write cause instead
of asserting the test leaked.

## Scope and safety

* **Caller-dependency sweep** — `_no_repo_root_leaks` is an autouse fixture with no callers.
  Nothing in the suite asserts the deletion: `git grep` over `_no_repo_root_leaks`,
  `repo_leak_snapshot`, `leak_failure_message` finds only the fixture, the `_isolation`
  primitives, this self-test, and the inline pytester copy — and that copy never deleted, so
  the guard's own end-to-end tests were already written against report-only semantics. Clear.
* **Restoration, not creation** — the change removes behaviour and corrects text. No new entry
  point, artifact, or mutating call.
* **No new dependency** — `import shutil` is removed, none added.
* **No test weakened** — no pre-existing assertion removed, loosened, skipped, or xfailed; the
  diff to existing tests is additive.

## Sibling sweep

* **Construct axis** — the class is "act destructively on shared-checkout state a snapshot
  diff cannot attribute". `grep` for `rmtree` / `.unlink()` across every `tests/**/conftest.py`
  finds exactly two other sites, and both are attributable: `conftest.py:380`
  (`_remove_readonly_run_snapshots`) deletes only under the test's own private `tmp_path`. No
  siblings.
* **Parity axis** — the rule is *a guard reading shared-checkout state must not act
  destructively on state it cannot attribute to the test*. Census of the guards that read
  shared checkout state: `_no_repo_root_leaks` (fixed); `pytest_sessionfinish` porcelain
  backstop (reports only — OK); `_no_repo_commits` (deletes nothing, but its remedy text ends
  in an unconditional `git reset --hard <sha>`, which is destructive advice given for a cause
  it cannot confirm — **MISSING**); `_remove_readonly_run_snapshots` and `_isolate_user_config`
  (N/A, `tmp_path`-scoped); the inline pytester copy in this self-test (N/A, never deleted).
  Disposition for the MISSING slot: filed as `hot-guessable-ungulate`
  (`a991-09dd-aa6a-4a27`), linked `discovered_from` this bug. Left out of this change
  deliberately — it is wording, not behaviour, and keeping this diff tight around the proven
  root cause is worth more than folding it in.

## Gates

* `make lint` — pass (ruff check + format-check + zizmor + actionlint).
* `make typecheck` — pass, 613 source files.
* `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` — `active=49 new=0 increased=0
  stale=0`. (The baseline covers `src/` only; a `tests/` change cannot disturb it.)
* **Full unit + scripts sweep**, CI selection and flags: **12978 passed, 46 skipped**, no
  failures, 8m16s.

## Gerrit

Change **1978** — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1978
